questions.correct: Angled rollers let the wheel slide sideways while pushing
wrong: Extra-large treads that grip the floor much harder
A tiny built-in motor inside each individual wheel
Sharp spikes that dig into the field tiles
questions.explain: Mecanum wheels have rollers set at 45°. Spinning the wheel still pushes forward, but the rollers let it slide sideways too — that's what enables strafing.

questions.q: What does "holonomic" mean for a drivetrain?
questions.correct: It can move any direction without turning first
wrong: It can only move forward and backward
It must spin before it can move at all
It drives about twice as fast as tank drive
questions.explain: Holonomic means the robot can go forward, backward, sideways, or diagonally without rotating first. Mecanum wheels make that possible.

questions.q: How must the four mecanum wheels be mounted?
questions.correct: In an X pattern, rollers pointing toward the center
wrong: In an O pattern, rollers pointing straight outward
All four wheels facing the exact same direction
Two facing forward and two turned sideways
questions.explain: The rollers must form an X (pointing toward center). An O pattern makes the robot fight itself and pull sideways instead of driving clean.

questions.correct: Moving straight sideways without rotating at all
wrong: Spinning quickly in place on one single spot
Driving forward while slowly turning to a side
Braking hard to stop the robot very fast
questions.explain: Strafing is pure sideways motion — the forward/back forces cancel and the sideways forces add up, so the robot slides left or right without turning.

questions.q: What are the three driver inputs for mecanum?
wrong: left power, right power, and a brake pedal
speed, gear, and a steering-wheel angle
intake, shooter, and hood angle settings
questions.explain: Mecanum mixes three inputs — drive (forward/back), strafe (sideways), and turn (spin) — into four separate wheel powers.

questions.q: In the mecanum mix, the drive term is...
questions.correct: Added to every wheel the exact same way
wrong: Subtracted from every one of the wheels
Only added to the two front wheels
Only used on the two left wheels
questions.explain: drive is + on all four wheels (so they all roll forward together). strafe alternates signs and turn is + on the left, - on the right.

questions.q: How does the strafe term's sign go across the wheels?
questions.correct: It alternates: plus, minus, minus, plus
wrong: It is plus on all four of the wheels
It is minus on all four of the wheels
It is only ever used on the back wheels
questions.explain: strafe is +−−+ across front-left, back-left, front-right, back-right. That alternating pattern is what slides the robot sideways.

questions.correct: Scaling all four powers down if any goes above 1.0
wrong: Rounding each of the four powers to the nearest whole number
Reversing the two left motors automatically
Turning off any wheel that spins too slowly
questions.explain: If any wheel power passes 1.0, you divide ALL four by the biggest one. That keeps their ratios (and the direction) intact instead of clipping one wheel.

questions.q: Why divide all wheels by the max instead of clamping each one?
questions.correct: To keep the direction ratios between the wheels correct
wrong: To make the robot drive noticeably faster overall
To save some battery by lowering every power
To reverse the robot's turning direction cleanly
questions.explain: Clamping wheels one at a time changes their ratios and bends the robot's direction. Dividing all four by the max shrinks them together, preserving the heading.

questions.q: A common way to set turn is...
wrong: left_stick_y minus right_stick_y
the A button minus the B button
left_bumper plus the right_bumper
questions.explain: turn = gamepad1.right_trigger - gamepad1.left_trigger. RT spins one way, LT the other, and the triggers are analog for gentle turns.

questions.q: Triggers report values in what range?
wrong: true or false
questions.explain: Triggers are analog from 0.0 (released) to 1.0 (fully squeezed). A light squeeze gives a gentle turn; a full squeeze turns hard.

questions.q: If strafing spins the robot instead of sliding, check...
questions.correct: The strafe signs — they should be plus, minus, minus, plus
wrong: The current battery voltage reading on the Control Hub before a match
The telemetry labels printed on each line
The name you gave your current code package
questions.explain: A spin on strafe usually means the +−−+ strafe signs are wrong for one or more wheels, so the sideways forces don't cancel the way they should.

questions.q: If the robot pulls to one side driving straight, the wheels may be...
questions.correct: In an O pattern instead of an X pattern
wrong: Spinning far too slowly to matter
Missing their encoder cables entirely
Set to the wrong telemetry label name
questions.explain: Rollers in an O pattern (pointing outward) make the robot fight itself and drift. Flip to the X pattern so the roller forces cooperate.

questions.q: The turn term is positive on the left wheels and...
wrong: Positive on the right wheels
Zero on the right wheels
Doubled on the right wheels
questions.explain: turn is + on the left, - on the right (like tank steering). That opposite pattern spins the robot in place.

questions.q: What lets a mecanum robot move diagonally?
questions.correct: Blending drive and strafe at the same time
wrong: Spinning only the two front wheels
Turning the wheels physically sideways
Reversing the battery's polarity briefly
questions.explain: Command drive and strafe together and the wheel mix blends them, so the robot glides diagonally — no turning required. That's the power of holonomic drive.
